# Bookself

> Bookself is open-source, Git-native publishing software for books, papers, course texts, and other long-form work. It keeps manuscripts as plain Markdown files, uses Git history for revision and review, separates private work-in-progress from public releases, and includes a browser Reader plus a Publishing Desk. The normal publishing path is local-first and does not require CI/CD.

Bookself's core lifecycle is: idea -> shape -> draft -> read -> revise -> review -> publish -> revise again.

The architecture has three roles:
- Platform: reusable Bookself software, templates, documentation, and setup tooling.
- Binder: a private Git repository for drafts, experiments, and the next edition.
- Shelf: a public Git repository containing intentionally released publication snapshots.

A Binder release copies a committed snapshot into the Shelf. Binder and Shelf are separate repositories with separate histories; the Shelf does not point back into the private Binder.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/README.md): project overview, concepts, workflow, examples, and neighboring tools.
- [Start Here](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/START-HERE.md): beginner path for authors who do not already know GitHub.
- [Publication template library](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books): blank starters for books, papers, magazines, newspapers, journals, newsletters, anthologies, reports, manuals/handbooks, and comics. In a real workflow these belong in the private Binder; a public Shelf should contain only intentionally released publications.
- [FAQ](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/faq.md): direct answers about Git-based books, version-controlled textbooks, Markdown papers, private/public publishing, CI/CD, interoperability, and comparisons with common alternatives.
- [Author guide](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/author-guide.md): writing and publishing workflow in plain language.
- [Bookself architecture](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/bookself.md): private Binder, public Shelf, release model, Reader, and Publishing Desk.
- [Writing lifecycle](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/writing-lifecycle.md): how software-development ideas map to books and papers.
- [Publication formats](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/publication-formats.md): books, papers, serials, comics, anthologies, reports/manuals, figures, and external web creations.
- [Revisions and releases](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/revisions.md): safe revision and edition workflow.
- [Editor guide](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/editor-guide.md): review and editing workflow.

## Academic and course-text writing

- [Academic writing](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/academic-writing.md): the supported plain-Markdown conventions for footnotes, citations and bibliography entries, semantic figure captions, numbered equations, and chapter-local references.
- [LaTeX math](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/latex.md): supported math delimiters and display environments for mathematical notation inside Markdown manuscripts.
- [Blank paper template](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/_PAPER_TEMPLATE): starter structure for a Markdown-first paper or research note.

The scholarly layer stays intentionally local-first: core Bookself does not require BibTeX/Biber, CSL, TeX packages, a hosted compiler, or CI. Agents should not invent those dependencies or claim book-wide reference semantics that the Reader does not provide.

## Compare alternatives

- [Bookself alternatives and neighboring tools](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/alternatives.md): practical comparisons with Overleaf, Manubot, Quarto, Jupyter Book, MyST Markdown, bookdown, Pressbooks, PubPub, Leanpub, GitBook, mdBook, Antora, Typst, Zettlr, HedgeDoc, and Pandoc.

Bookself's closest conceptual neighbor is Manubot because both use Git and Markdown as useful infrastructure for scholarly writing. Bookself differentiates around an approachable publication lifecycle, general books and papers, local-first release tooling, an explicit private Binder/public Shelf boundary, and a Reader plus Publishing Desk.

## Cite Bookself

- [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/CITATION.cff): machine-readable software citation metadata for Bookself.

No DOI or semantic version is claimed unless the project actually publishes one. Cite the specific repository commit in addition to the citation metadata when reproducibility requires an exact software revision.

## Examples

- [How to Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/how-to-bookself): short practical guide built as a Bookself publication.
- [Bookself 101](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-101): academic textbook example with learning objectives, key terms, discussion questions, labs, and semester editions.
- [Making Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/making-bookself): intentionally unfinished public Binder-style teaching specimen that dogfoods the Bookself improvement loop.
- [Public Shelf implementation](https://github.com/Svyable/shelf): example public release repository.
- [Public Reader](https://svyable.github.io/shelf/reader/): live Bookself Shelf reader.

## Live recursive improvement loop

Use this when the request is broad, exploratory, or asks how Bookself itself could improve:

1. [Read the Making Bookself working proof](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/reader/#/b/making-bookself/) as a reader.
2. [Read its review map](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/books/making-bookself/REVIEW.md) for active questions and the distinction between personal notes, shared review feedback, and source changes.
3. [Read the public review thread](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/35).
4. Read `AGENTS.md` before modifying the repository.
5. Choose one bounded improvement, verify the relevant behavior, and leave a durable explanation in the commit or pull request.
6. Compare the working-proof experience with the [released Shelf Reader](https://svyable.github.io/shelf/reader/).

The target loop is: read -> locate -> understand -> propose -> review -> revise -> read again. The public specimen is intentionally visible for teaching; real Binders should remain private.

## For contributors and agents

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/AGENTS.md): repository architecture, invariants, editing rules, and cross-agent instructions.
- [.github/copilot-instructions.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/.github/copilot-instructions.md): GitHub Copilot repository onramp.
- [.github/instructions/publications.instructions.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/.github/instructions/publications.instructions.md): path-specific publication editing rules for GitHub agents.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): contribution workflow.

Important constraints:
- Keep books and papers as plain files under books/.
- Do not require CI/CD for the private Binder authoring or release path.
- Shared UI is reader/ and desk/; instance identity belongs in imprint.json.
- Do not hard-code an author's private repository or identity into shared UI.
- The framework is MIT licensed; publication manuscripts retain their authors' copyright.
